post_topic: Unowned cloud spend and ungoverned infrastructure access as slow-burn budget and audit risk
scene_description: A split-scene showing the hidden sprawl of ungoverned cloud infrastructure: on one side, a tidy project roadmap marked 'shipped' with engineers walking away, and on the other, a chaotic tangle of persistent AWS IAM roles, idle S3 buckets, and orphaned service accounts still running months later with no owner assigned. In the foreground, Kelvin Davis — a Black/African American man in his late 30s to 40 years old with short hair greying at the temples and a short neatly trimmed beard — reviews a cost allocation dashboard that shows steadily climbing cloud bills, each line item just below the threshold that would trigger a conversation. The tension lies between the clean story the roadmap tells and the ungoverned reality still accumulating costs and access risk in the background.
